Guides

Choosing ingredients

Variety, bitter greens included, matters more than an organic label. Only a short list of foods is genuinely unsuitable.

Key points

Offer bitter and savoury flavours early. Babies who try green vegetables in the first weeks of solids are more willing to eat them later.
Put an iron-rich food on your first shopping list. The practical sources are meat, lentils, beans, tofu, and fortified baby cereal.
A short list of foods to avoid is enough. Honey, added salt, added sugar, rice drinks, whole nuts, unpasteurised dairy, and a few kinds of fish are the ones with a real reason behind them.

Variety, including the tricky flavours

ESPGHAN recommends a range of flavours and textures, bitter greens included. A month of nothing but sweet pear and banana teaches a narrow palate. Broccoli, spinach mixed into something, beans, and fish can all appear in the first two weeks.

Organic produce hasn’t been shown to change allergy or growth in babies. Wash it, and peel it if the skin is tough or very dirty. Eating in season is a pleasure and saves money, but it isn’t a safety rule.

Build around iron

It helps to keep one iron-rich food ready: cooked mince in the freezer, red lentils in the cupboard, unsalted beans, eggs, or a fortified cereal whose taste you can live with. Serve plant iron with fruit or pepper for vitamin C.

Rice cereal is optional. It isn’t needed for sleep or as a first spoonful, and rice drinks are a different product altogether. Children under five shouldn’t have rice drinks, because of arsenic.

Foods to skip or change, and why

Honey, even baked, can contain spores that cause infant botulism. It waits until after the first birthday, and even then it’s still sugar. Salt waits too: a baby’s daily limit is under 1 gram, which ordinary foods already provide, so none is added, and stock cubes, ham, and soy sauce stay out. Sugar and fruit juice aren’t needed; give the fruit itself.

Whole nuts, whole grapes, popcorn, and hard dried fruit are choking hazards. Shark, swordfish, and marlin contain too much mercury. Unpasteurised milk and mould-ripened cheeses can carry listeria. Undercooked kidney beans and other dried beans can make you ill quickly; boil them until completely soft. Liver is nutritious, but so high in vitamin A that one small portion a week is the limit.
